title: Autopilot recommender for batching + cache with progressive rollouts and SLI-driven analysis dashboard
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and run a rigorous experimentation program to validate an automated recommender that proposes batching and KV cache configuration changes and a safe, progressive apply/rollback mechanism. The goal is to measure cost savings without degrading latency SLAs or output quality and to ship dashboards and alerts that let operators trust autopilot changes in production.
background: We currently have heuristics and manual playbooks for batching and prefix/KV caching. Teams want a recommender to suggest config deltas (batch_size, max_batch_ms, cache_prefetch_limits, min_batch_threshold) and an automated, guarded apply path that can progressively roll configs to cohorts and rollback on safety signals. Prior tickets explored AB frameworks and safety gates; this ticket stitches recommender logic with rollout policies and observability instrumentation.
acceptance_criteria: Autopilot recommender prototype outputs ranked config suggestions for a given route/workload with expected cost delta and expected P95 impact
Progressive rollout flow implemented: canary -> 5% cohort -> 25% cohort -> global with automated rollback triggers
Define and surface primary SLIs (cost per 1k tokens, P95 latency, tail error rate, quality-regression-score) on a dashboard and alerting rules for breach
Statistical test plan and power calculations documented; minimum detectable uplift for cost set to 5% with 80% power for target routes
Run experiment for 3 representative workloads and produce a runbook with decision criteria to promote recommender to self-apply in non-critical routes
experiment_design_summary: Randomized cohort assignment per route keyed by customer_id (or session_id for anonymous routes). Control uses current config; treatment applies recommender suggestion. Each experiment runs for a minimum of 72 hours with daily snapshots. Safety gates evaluate continuously and will trigger immediate rollback for any cohort when thresholds are exceeded.
primary_metrics: P95_latency_ms: must not increase beyond 7% relative
tail_error_rate (% requests with model or runtime errors): must remain <= baseline + 0.05 percentage points
kv_cache_hit_rate: expected direction up or neutral
quality_regression_score (automated evals on holdout prompt set): must not degrade beyond 1.5% absolute
safety_gates_and_thresholds: Immediate rollback if P95_latency_ms increase > 15% within any 30-minute window
Immediate rollback if tail_error_rate increases > 0.2 percentage points over baseline within one hour
Pause rollout to next cohort if cost savings are < 1% after 24 hours for that cohort
Abort promotion and mark recommender as unsafe for route if automated eval quality_regression_score drops > 1.5% after 48 hours
statistical_plan: We will use two-sided t-tests on log-transformed cost-per-token and a non-parametric Mann-Whitney U for latency percentiles. Power calc example: to detect a 5% cost reduction at alpha=0.05 and power=0.8 with assumed sigma=12% requires ~1,600 samples per cohort for high-throughput routes. For low-throughput routes we will increase cohort duration or use hierarchical pooling across similar routes.
dashboard_requirements: Per-route cohort view showing cost_per_1k, P50/P95 latency, error rate, kv hit rate, and quality_regression_score
Cohort-level trend charts with confidence intervals and annotation of canary/promotion events
Traffic allocation over time with ability to force rollback from dashboard
Alerting widgets tied to safety gate thresholds and an incident playbook link
monitoring_implementation_notes: Instrument sampling to tag requests with cohort_id and autopilot_config_id. Emit a unified experiment event with cost, latency, error, kv_hit boolean, and evaluation_score for a small eval cohort. Ensure these telemetry fields feed into existing tracing pipelines and a new experiment metrics index to avoid noisy joins.
rollout_workflow: 1) Generate ranked suggestions and estimated deltas; 2) Run offline replay on recent traffic for quick simulation; 3) Launch canary (1% traffic) for 24h with full telemetry; 4) If gates pass, promote to 5% for 48h then 25% for 72h; 5) Global if all cohorts pass. At any gate failure, auto-rollback to previous config and record a rollback reason in the experiment log.
